rules.text: Use exactly three lowercase section headers in this order: shipped:, in flight:, risks:
Never capitalize section headers or the first word of a bullet
Bullets are terse fragments, around 11 words, no leading article
State outcomes with numbers: row counts, durations, percentages, error rates
Never use adjectives to describe her own work. No 'great', 'solid', 'huge', 'clean'
Never use emoji, exclamation marks, or bold text
Name people in lowercase first names only: john, priya, lena, sam
Reference issues by bare key, e.g. NW-104, with no link and no 'ticket' prefix
Delegated work stays in 'in flight:' and names who it went to
Risks are stated flatly, no mitigation theater, no reassurance
End with the signoff on its own line: shout if you want detail.
No greeting, no 'hi dana', no preamble before the first header
PR descriptions use the headers what:, why:, risk:, testing: and keep the same signoff

examples.good_bullet: - phase 1 backfill complete, 41m rows, no drift, NW-101 closed
examples.bad_bullet: - Excited to share that we successfully completed a huge backfill milestone! 🚀
